name: Abū Saʿīd al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Marzubān al-Sīrāfī
summary: Basran grammarian and Ḥanafī judge of Baghdad, author of the great commentary on Sībawayh's al-Kitāb and of the first history of the Basran grammarians; remembered for his debate with the logician Mattā.
bio: Al-Sīrāfī was born in Sīrāf on the Persian Gulf, studied in Oman and ʿAskar Mukram and settled in Baghdad, where he read grammar with Ibn al-Sarrāj and Ibn Durayd and served as deputy judge. Al-Zubaydī, his contemporary, describes him in the tenth Basran generation: the man who explained Sībawayh's book, who laid claim to the Almagest, Euclid and logic, who followed Abū Ḥanīfa in law and lived in al-Ruṣāfa. The sources add that he lived from copying books and would eat only what he had earned by his own hand.

His Sharḥ Kitāb Sībawayh, many volumes long, became the standard commentary on al-Kitāb. His Akhbār al-naḥwiyyīn al-Baṣriyyīn, the reports of the Basran grammarians, is the oldest of the ṭabaqāt works that survive: from Abū al-Aswad to the teachers of his own time, with their teachers, students and anecdotes.

In 326/938, at the court of the vizier Ibn al-Furāt, he debated the Christian logician Abū Bishr Mattā, who held that logic was needed to tell sound speech from faulty. Al-Sīrāfī answered that logic was the grammar of Greek and that sense in Arabic was weighed by the grammar of Arabic. The debate is known from Abū Ḥayyān al-Tawḥīdī's report of it, which leaves al-Sīrāfī the winner. He died in Baghdad in 368/979.

works.title: Akhbār al-naḥwiyyīn al-Baṣriyyīn
works.note: The oldest surviving ṭabaqāt of the grammarians.
